newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar tumbles on Birch comments.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar tumbles on Birch comments.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar tumbled sharply after the close on Monday on comments from Finance Minister Bill Birch that he expects further weakness.
At 6.25 p.m. (0625 GMT) it was at US$0.6445/52 after the local market had closed at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at 0.6482/89, having started the session at 0.6520/27.
The Trade-Weighted Index fell to 64.38 from 64.89.
An Auckland dealer said Birch had not said anything particularly new but signalled approval of the the ower level.
He expects U.S. investors to try and push it lower.
"It's going to be hard for the kiwi to rally over 0.6480-0.6500 from here," he said.
Birch said he expected the kiwi to come down.
"They (the Reserve Bank of New Zealand) are foreshadowing further easings towards the end of this year so you are likely to get a little more easing," he told Reuters in Melbourne.
Birch said he was more comfortable with where the currency was today than where it was last week.
The New Zealand dollar has fallen sharply in recent weeks after a period in which it has been perceived as over-valued.
"From the point of view of the mix between interest rates and exchange rates the rebalancing has been very positive, I think, in terms of long term growth," Birch said.
The local market had already left the kiwi on its session low and looking weak.

"It's not got any strength. It's finishing on its lows and it looks like it could head a little lower overnight. It's still got no rallying ability," a Wellington bank dealer said before Birch's comments.
There was importer interest in the morning to sell the New Zealand dollar against the yen and mark.
Pressure was also exerted on the kiwi from a weak Australian dollar, which failed to rally despite the failure of an expected rate cut to materialise as yet.
Earlier, Macquarie Bank Chief Economist Bill Shields told Reuters Financial TV that he expects an upward correction in the New Zealand dollar.
"We think we've seen close to the bottom and we would expect the New Zealand dollar to appreciate, one or two cents, over the next three to six months."
He expects bill yields to rally to more realistic levels.
"We don't doubt that the economy may be very close to the bottom in New Zealand but we don't see a very rapid recovery. We see a drawn-out recovery over the next year or two."
Shields said the New Zealand dollar could revisit its lower levels if there was further uncertainty about the policy outlook.
He expects the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to condone a further easing in monetary conditions in the next three and six months "and probably much more than currently in prospect".
